title: docs: give postgres/mysql the same optional-driver note Turso has
body:
Fixes #14551

## What changed

`content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` — the `OS_DATABASE_URL` row already
carried an optional-package note for `libsql://` / Turso but not for
`postgres://…` / `mysql://…`, even though `pg`, `mysql2` and `tedious` are all
declared `optional: true` peer dependencies of `@objectstack/driver-sql`
(`packages/drivers/driver-sql/package.json:32-37` — verified on this branch's
base, `origin/main` `53d368921`). The row now reads (new clauses only):

> `postgres://…`'s driver is an **optional** package too — `npm install pg`,
> or the boot fails loudly rather than degrading to SQLite

> its driver is likewise an **optional** package — `npm install mysql2`, or
> the boot fails loudly rather than degrading to SQLite

— same wording pattern as the existing Turso clause, same row (kept as one
table cell, no line breaks).

The bare-Node (systemd) recipe on the same page installs only the CLI; it now
also installs the driver:

```bash
npm install -g @objectstack/cli
npm install -g pg   # Postgres driver is an optional peer of @objectstack/driver-sql —
                    # install it next to the CLI, or the boot fails loudly (use mysql2 for OS_DATABASE_URL=mysql://…)
scp dist/objectstack.json server:/opt/my-app/objectstack.json
```

I did not assert a specific global-npm resolution mechanism (e.g. "the CLI
resolves `pg` from the global `node_modules`") — I could confirm that
`@objectstack/driver-sql` never `require`s/`import`s `pg` directly (it hands
`client: 'pg'` to `knex`, which does its own driver resolution;
`git grep -n "from 'pg'\|require('pg')\|import('pg')" packages/drivers/driver-sql/src`
returns nothing), but I have no way in this container to run a real global
npm install and observe `knex`'s resolution against it. The recipe step is
phrased generically ("install it next to the CLI") rather than claiming a
resolution mechanism I did not measure, per this card's own instruction.

`content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` — the "needs one extra install"
callout is Turso-only, and the `URL → Driver Inference Table`'s `postgres://…`
/ `mysql://…` rows named the peer package (`+ pg`, `+ mysql2`) without saying
it's not installed by default or that boot fails loudly — the same gap in a
milder form. Smallest-edit fix: extended those two rows with
`(**optional** peer — install it yourself, or boot fails loudly)`, matching
the Turso row's `(**optional** — install it yourself)` pattern. Left the
"Supported Drivers" table's `peer: pg` / `peer: mysql2` notation and the
callout itself alone — the inference table is the first place a reader lands
and is now consistent across all three optional-driver rows.

## Out of scope (left for #14510)

No packaging change: no `package.json` dependency moves, no Dockerfile /
Compose edits, no scaffolder changes. The container recipes on this same page
(`postgres://` examples in the Docker/Compose/K8s sections) are untouched —
the row's note is what covers them for a reader who follows the link back up.

## Docs-only

No changeset (`skip-changeset` label applied) — prose-only change to two
`content/docs/**` pages.
